DOID:0050553.definition: A proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome that is characterized by early childhood onset of annular erythematous plaques on the face and extremities with subsequent development of partial lipodystrophy and laboratory evidence of immune dysregulation and that has_material_basis_in homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PSMB8 gene on chromosome 6p21. Digenic forms of PRAAS1 can be caused by heterozygous mutation in the PSMB8 gene and heterozygous mutation in either the PSMA3 gene on chromosome 14q23 or in the PSMB4 on chromosome 1q21.

curated_candidates.name: PTCH1-related nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome
SUFU-related nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome

has_subtypes.description: The predominant form (~85-95% of cases), caused by germline PTCH1 mutations. Characterized by high rates of basal cell carcinomas, odontogenic keratocysts, skeletal anomalies, and calcification of the falx cerebri. Medulloblastoma risk is low (<2%). Many individuals have a recognizable facial appearance. Missense variants are associated with later diagnosis and milder phenotype.

evidence.explanation: GeneReviews characterizes recognizable facial appearance in PTCH1-related NBCCS as common ("many individuals") without specifying a proportion; the unsourced "~60%" figure was removed to match the cited evidence.
evidence.snippet: Many individuals have a recognizable appearance with macrocephaly, frontal bossing, coarse facial features, and facial milia.

has_subtypes.name: PTCH1-related

has_subtypes.description: A minority form (~5% of cases), caused by germline SUFU mutations. Characterized by milder BCC burden, absence of jaw keratocysts, but markedly higher risk of medulloblastoma (up to 33%), meningioma (~11%), and gonadal tumors. Facial features are subtler. Often presents in early childhood with medulloblastoma.

evidence.explanation: GeneReviews quantifies the 33% medulloblastoma penetrance for SUFU pathogenic variant carriers versus <2% for PTCH1, directly supporting the comparative risk figures in the SUFU-related subtype description.
evidence.snippet: The risk of developing medulloblastoma is substantially higher in individuals with an SUFU pathogenic variant (33%) than in those with a PTCH1 pathogenic variant (<2%).

evidence.explanation: In this scoping review of 176 confirmed SUFU+/- carriers, meningioma occurred in 19 patients (19/176 ≈ 11%), supporting the ~11% meningioma figure in the SUFU-related subtype description.
evidence.reference_title: Medulloblastoma and other neoplasms in patients with heterozygous germline SUFU variants: A scoping review.
evidence.snippet: the most common were medulloblastoma (N = 59 patients), BCC (N = 21 patients), and meningioma (N = 19 patients)

has_subtypes.name: SUFU-related

mondo_mappings.mapping_justification: Orphanet lists MONDO:0007187 as an exact cross-reference for the ORPHA:377 Gorlin syndrome record.

omimps_mappings.mapping_justification: PS109400 encompasses basal cell nevus syndrome types 1 and 2, represented here as PTCH1-related and SUFU-related subtypes of Gorlin syndrome. Loss of Hedgehog-pathway restraint provides a shared mechanism, while genotype-specific tumor risks remain distinct within the entry. The January 2026 OMIM snapshot contains OMIM:109400 and OMIM:620343; the September 2026 MONDO snapshot maps MONDO:0007187 exactly to the series and has the corresponding two subtype children. This is a syndrome-level alignment, not an assertion that the clinical manifestations or tumor risks are identical across genotypes, nor a mapping to sporadic basal cell carcinoma or to every SUFU-associated tumor predisposition phenotype.
